items.picture: At a newspaper kiosk on a street corner, magazines hanging all round its window, Emma buys a newspaper from the vendor and tucks it under her arm.
In the café near the university, Emma spreads the newspaper on the table and reads an article, a finger following the lines, her coffee going cold beside her.
Evening in the porter's lodge: pán Kováč watches the news on a small TV, a newsreader at a desk on the screen, a mug of tea in his hand.
At the newspaper kiosk, Lucia takes a glossy magazine off the rack and flips through its colourful pages.

items.text: Emma číta slovenské noviny. = Emma is reading a Slovak newspaper.
šport a kultúra = sport and culture
items.picture: Two halves, as if two newspaper pages came to life. Left: an ice hockey player shoots the puck into the net. Right: a violinist plays on a concert stage under a spotlight.
The weather page of the newspaper, open on the dorm kitchen table: a map of Slovakia covered in little sun, cloud, rain and snow symbols. Emma studies it over breakfast.
Tomáš on the same park bench as in the other weather pictures, under a thick grey sky with no sun at all, zipping up his hoodie.

items.text: Je teplo. Je zima. = It's warm. It's cold.
items.picture: Two halves. Left: Emma in a T-shirt and sunglasses fans herself on the sunny Danube embankment. Right: Emma, bundled up in a woolly hat and scarf, shivers on a snowy mountain path in the Tatras.
At the dorm kitchen table, Lucia reads the small-ads page of the newspaper, a grid of little boxed ads, and circles one in red pen.

items.text: Firma hľadá programátora. = A company is looking for a programmer.
items.picture: Emma, reading the small ads, points out one with a little drawing of a person at a computer; Tomáš leans over her shoulder, interested.

items.text: You want to know the weather. What do you ask?
Emma tells her friend Lucia “You're in the paper!” Which is right?
items.picture: Emma bursts into the dorm kitchen waving the newspaper, open at a page with a photo of Lucia; Lucia, mid-bite of toast, stares at it in surprise.

items.text: You meet your teacher, pani Horváthová. What do you say?
Emma is from Ireland. How does she say it?
